entry.title: v0.10.12 — Catalogue: five more "stub" leads settled
entry.summary: Five more leads of the catalogue marked "stub" (unsourced notes) are settled, each with its source or its reason. Lead M (BHV, Bilu–Hanrot–Voutier): withdrawn: a first application (April 2026) had been refuted (mea culpa #11), the "specific applications" of the later reopening were never stated, and we found no source linking this theorem to cycles (dead end in the table, 4-test "—", reference of the paper added). Lead R (statistical invariants): dead end with no source of its own; same reason as lead C: these invariants depend only on the parity word, and every word is that of a rational cycle (Halbeisen and Hungerbühler, Acta Arith. 78 (1997), Lemma 2 and §5). Lead H (model-theoretic logic): dead end, now sourced: Cobham (1969); Villemaire (1992), the theory of ⟨ℕ, +, V₂, V₃⟩ is undecidable; two 2026 preprints (arXiv:2601.12772, arXiv:2602.06066) according to which the iteration of 3x+1 is not definable in Büchi arithmetic in base 2, nor reachability in base 3. Lead H.1 (MSO / Skolem–Bruyère): dead end instead of "Unexplored", same sources and Bruyère, Hansel, Michaux and Villemaire (1994). Lead H.2 (Skolem–Mahler–Lech / Derksen): dead end, now sourced (Lech 1953, Derksen 2007): the 3x+1 map is not linear, and the orbit of a cycle is a trivial linear recurrence. Corrections to v0.10.11: the entry for lead K wrongly said the lead had never been written up (an April 2026 analysis exists, without a source linking cycles to Faltings's theorem; outcome unchanged), and the entry for lead C now restricts its "discrete Fourier" remark to the April 2026 reports we re-read. Counters: 11 stub notes out of 36 instead of 16; card B of the hypotheses: 12 of 16 dead-ends in Region II instead of 11, estimate unchanged; "Latest audit" card: internal AI-assisted adversarial review (not peer review) of the changes of this version.

entry.title: v0.10.11 — Catalogue: five "stub" leads settled
entry.summary: The first five leads of the catalogue marked "stub" (unsourced notes) are settled, each with its source or its reason. Lead C (discrete Fourier / Sturmian): dead end, now sourced: Fernández and Ibáñez (arXiv:2607.24844, 2026 preprint) link Christoffel words and cycles through size estimates, and Halbeisen and Hungerbühler (Acta Arith. 78 (1997), Lemma 2 and §5) note that such estimates, valid for rational cycles, cannot on their own exclude integer cycles; the "discrete Fourier" part is withdrawn, as the name of the lead now says. Lead E.4 (Zudilin 2007, J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 19): dead end instead of "partial": its bound concerns ‖(3/2)^k‖ and gives no more than 2^(k−1) for 2^S − 3^k this way. Lead F renamed "Marcovecchio 2014": no paper from 2025 was found; the author's only text dated 2025 is the arXiv deposit of a 2014 paper (Int. J. Number Theory 10), whose measures concern a logarithm such as log 2, not S ln 2 − k ln 3: dead end. Lead J (tropical, suggested by an AI assistant): dead end with no published source; the lab's check of the tropicalisation of the cycle equation (2026-09-26) gives back the starting congruence. Lead K (arithmetic schemes + Faltings): withdrawn, unsourced (dead end in the table; dashed node in the lock diagram). Counters: 16 stub notes out of 36 instead of 21. Home page: the count "fourteen of the fifteen paradigms" of the lock diagram is dated to April 2026 and said to be under review, and the caption no longer gives a number (node "Schemes + Faltings" dashed, node "Marcovecchio 2014"); card C of the hypotheses carries the same mention, its estimate unchanged; "Latest audit" card: internal AI-assisted adversarial review (not peer review) of the changes of this version.

entry.title: v0.10.10 — Steiner 1978 in Lean 4
entry.summary: Steiner 1978 formalised in Lean 4 (release v1.2, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23541611): a formalisation of a classical theorem from 1978; the only circuit on the positive integers that is a cycle of the 3x+1 map is {1, 2}, here proved under a named hypothesis (Rhin's bound, H_Rhin, never an axiom) and without any hypothesis for at most 20,000 odd terms. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles. The statements and the proof were written without the original paper (Congr. Numer. 20, 1978): they are reconstructed from Steiner 1981, Lagarias's annotated bibliography and Simons–de Weger 2005 (read in their version 1.44 of 2010). After release v1.2, on 2026-10-21, the paper was read in a scanned copy and compared with the statements: nothing in the Lean files changes. 12 frozen statements, all proved; standard axioms only. The bound for 20,000 odd terms is far weaker than those that rely on a computer verification of the conjecture. Submitted to ccchallenge ("Ready to be audited"). Papers page: new Steiner 1978 card; home page: "Latest milestone" and "Last Lean verification" cards on Steiner 1978, "Latest audit" card: internal AI-assisted adversarial review (not peer review) of the changes of this version; History: the October 2026 entry cites Steiner 1978; research ledger: one event dated 2026-10-21 (34 events, 25 milestones).

entry.title: v0.10.9 — Re-check of no_cycle_k_le_1322, errata note
entry.summary: Errata note on Halbeisen–Hungerbühler 1997 and Lagarias 1990 (Zenodo, 2026-10-21, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23535498): 9 and 21 points, each checked by a Lean theorem or by a script. None of them invalidates a theorem that we formalised. The list is not exhaustive. The two wrong rows of Lagarias's Table 3.1 (k = 35 and k = 73) were already corrected in the OEIS (A102280, A102284; G. H. Morley, 2013). Research ledger: two events dated 2026-10-21 (33 events, 24 milestones); the labels of its counters are now shown in one language only; "Latest audit" card: internal AI-assisted adversarial review (not peer review) of the changes of this version; Papers page: the errata note is mentioned in the introduction. The mentions saying that no_cycle_k_le_1322 was not re-checked are updated; no_nontrivial_cycle_phase59, no_cycle_k_gt_1322, sdw_from_cf, δ10, δ11 and CGS-7, among others, are still not re-checked. On 20–21 October 2026, the 35 Lean files of release v1.0 that make up the import closure of Phase58PorteDeuxFinal.lean (which contains no_cycle_k_le_1322) were re-checked on Lean 4.34.0, which includes the fix of lean4#14576: they compile, and no_cycle_k_le_1322 depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Phase59–63 and PhaseVIII, hence no_nontrivial_cycle_phase59, were not re-checked. Details and limits: https://github.com/ericmerle3789/collatz-conditional-cycles/tree/main/recheck-v4.34-2026-10-20

entry.title: v0.10.8 — Seven open items closed
entry.summary: Seven open items of the site closed after checks against the available sources. δ10 withdrawn (outdated cartography): its conditions (1) and (3), defined on the Papers page, concern replacing BakerSeparation, which the k ≤ 1322 result does not need, since Hercher 2023 with Bařina's verification already implies it. The "impossibility trilogy" announcement withdrawn: δ8 and δ8′ restate a remark of Halbeisen and Hungerbühler (1997, §5); the proof sketch of Lemma 5.1 of the PDF is withdrawn. Tests REQ-MATH-004 and REQ-MATH-012 withdrawn. Studies closed: Eliahou-Steiner decomposition (closed: it formalised no theorem of Eliahou's; Eliahou's bound, as restated by Halbeisen–Hungerbühler, is proved in hh1997/), partial replacement of the Baker hypothesis (dead end), Knight 2026 (reading closed, dead end for this project) and Calegari–Dimitrov–Tang 2025 (reading closed, dead end for this project as things stand; abstract only). Home page: card A′ keeps its April 2026 estimate (8-12%), with a dated note (also on the History timeline); card B corrected to 11 of 16 dead-ends in Region II (estimate unchanged); "Latest audit" card: internal AI-assisted adversarial review (not peer review) of the seven closures; Papers page: closed or withdrawn cards are kept for the record, each with its status. entry.title: v0.10.6 — δ11 withdrawn
entry.summary: δ11 (delta11_salikhov_insufficient, Phase 65, k in [3694, 3732]) is withdrawn: it rested on transposing Salikhov's 2007 irrationality measure of ln 3 to a problem about log₂ 3, and on an ad hoc axiom not taken from the paper; Salikhov's bound holds only beyond unspecified heights, so no explicit threshold follows (erratum of the Zenodo v4 version, item 3). Marked "withdrawn" on every page, with the reason and a link to the withdrawal note (https://github.com/ericmerle3789/collatz-conditional-cycles/blob/study/E1-salikhov-2007-impossibility/RETRAIT_DELTA11_2026-10-20.md); nothing erased; δ10 not affected.

entry.title: v0.10.2 — Aligned with the Zenodo v4 version (erratum)
entry.summary: Version v4 of the preprint on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23496480) keeps the PDF of 27 April 2026 and adds a 2-page erratum; the site no longer says the PDF still carries the old statement. Item 1 of the erratum: in Lean, k is any return time, so under H2 the hypothesis H3 excludes every non-trivial cycle on its own, as does ProductBoundThreshold; both are equivalent to the conclusion (the earlier wording "for k > 1322" was too weak). What is proved without circularity is unchanged: no non-trivial cycle with k ≤ 1322, under H1 and H2. The thresholds k ≤ 3693 and k ≤ 3732 are withdrawn; δ8 is credited to a remark of Halbeisen–Hungerbühler 1997 (§5).

entry.title: v0.10.0 — Halbeisen–Hungerbühler 1997 in Lean 4
entry.summary: Formalisation in Lean 4.34.0 (Mathlib v4.34.0) of a classical paper, not a new result: L. Halbeisen and N. Hungerbühler, "Optimal bounds for the length of rational Collatz cycles", Acta Arithmetica 78 (1997), 227-239. Everything the paper proves is kernel-checked, with the finite verification behind the example of §4.4 (if the conjecture is verified up to 212,366,032,807,211, every cycle of integers not containing 1 has at least 102,225,496 elements); 70 statements frozen before their proofs, 0 sorry, 0 native_decide, standard axioms only; not proved: the 1/2 bound of Remark 1, which the paper does not prove. Code: https://github.com/ericmerle3789/one-obstruction-three-faces-lean/tree/36d5136/hh1997
